subject: Nanotechnology
title: The Birth of DNA Origami
description: Learn The Birth of DNA Origami in one minute.

hook.text: In 2006, Paul Rothemund folded a single long DNA strand into a smiley face — DNA origami was born.

buildup.text: A 7000-base scaffold strand is folded by 200 short staple strands — each staple pins distant scaffold regions together.

discovery.text: The design is computational — software calculates where each staple binds to fold the scaffold into any 2D shape.

twist.text: Mix scaffold and staples, heat, and cool — the structure folds itself in one pot with no enzymes or machines.

climax.text: DNA origami achieves 6 nm resolution — each staple places a feature with near-atomic spatial precision.

punchline.text: DNA writes code — but Rothemund showed it also folds into shapes.

quiz.question: How does DNA origami create specific shapes?
options: Enzymes cut DNA into the desired shape like molecular scissors
Short staple strands pin distant regions of a long scaffold strand together, folding it into a designed shape
DNA molecules naturally fold into predetermined geometric forms
